question: What is the main job of Waldeyer's ring in the body?

options.A: Secreting hormones to control overall body temperature
options.B: Regulating airflow into the lower respiratory tract
options.C: Producing digestive enzymes to break down food proteins
options.D: Catching germs entering through the nose and mouth

explanation: Waldeyer's ring is a protective ring of tissue that catches germs coming in through breathing or swallowing before they can travel deeper into the body. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T4#BMP111_U6_T4_h1)

question: Which of these structures is also commonly called the adenoids?
explanation: The pharyngeal tonsils are located in the roof of the nasopharynx and are frequently referred to as the adenoids, especially when they swell in children. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T4#BMP111_U6_T4_h1)

question: Where are the palatine tonsils found in the mouth and throat?

options.A: At the very base of the back third of the tongue
options.B: Between the arches of the soft palate
options.C: High up on the roof of the back of the nose
options.D: Directly surrounding the opening of the Eustachian tube

explanation: The palatine tonsils sit on the side walls of the throat right between the two arches of the soft palate. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T4#BMP111_U6_T4_h2)

question: Why can swollen pharyngeal tonsils make it hard to breathe through the nose?

options.A: They block the airway at the back of the nose
options.B: They press downward on the windpipe
options.C: They prevent the vocal cords from opening during sleep
options.D: They swell so large that they push the tongue backward

explanation: Because the pharyngeal tonsils sit in the upper airway, when they enlarge they block air from passing freely from the nose down into the throat. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T4#BMP111_U6_T4_h2)

question: What feature of the tonsils helps increase their surface area to catch incoming germs?
explanation: Deep folds called tonsillar crypts create a large surface area where foreign particles and bacteria get trapped so immune cells can find them. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T4#BMP111_U6_T4_h3)

question: Which antibody type is produced locally by tonsil tissue to protect moist body linings?
explanation: Immune tissues in the throat produce secretory IgA to defend the moist linings of the body against invading microbes. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T4#BMP111_U6_T4_h3)

question: Which bacterium is most commonly linked to acute bacterial tonsillitis (strep throat)?
explanation: Infections caused by Group A beta-hemolytic Streptococcus are the most frequent bacterial cause of acute tonsillitis requiring antibiotics. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T4#BMP111_U6_T4_h4)

question: What is a peritonsillar abscess, also known as quinsy?

options.A: A benign tumor growing on the surface of the tonsils
options.B: Permanent scarring of the tonsil folds after a viral infection
options.C: A collection of pus between the tonsil and the throat wall
options.D: Complete destruction of the tongue tonsils from chronic inflammation

explanation: Quinsy occurs when an infection spreads past the tonsil, creating a painful pocket of pus that pushes the tonsil out of its normal position. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T4#BMP111_U6_T4_h4)

question: What does it usually mean if one tonsil is much bigger than the other during an exam?

options.A: Normal variation in a healthy adult
options.B: The early stages of a simple cold
options.D: A potential abscess or underlying growth

explanation: When one tonsil is significantly larger than the other, it serves as a warning sign for a localized pocket of pus or a growth rather than a standard balanced infection. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T4#BMP111_U6_T4_h5)

question: A child has a muffled voice, severe throat pain, and drools because swallowing hurts. What condition should the midwife suspect?
explanation: A muffled voice and an inability to swallow saliva leading to drooling are classic signs of a peritonsillar abscess that requires urgent medical referral. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T4#BMP111_U6_T4_h5)

question: Why might a patient feel ear pain after having their tonsils removed?

options.A: Surgical instruments damage the outer ear canal
options.B: Nerves shared between the throat and ear cause referred pain
options.C: Blood from the throat pools inside the middle ear
options.D: Ear infections always develop after anesthesia

explanation: The throat and the ear share nerve pathways, so healing tissue in the throat area often causes harmless referred pain that is felt in the ears. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T4#BMP111_U6_T4_h6)

question: What is an early sign that a patient is quietly bleeding in the throat after tonsil surgery?
explanation: When blood trickles down the back of the throat after surgery, the patient tends to swallow it repeatedly, making frequent swallowing an important early clue. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T4#BMP111_U6_T4_h6)
